A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. Content can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F report original synthetic experiments, prediction results on sushi, jokes, Netflix and MovieLens data, and a welfare-maximization analysis.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, and Appendix F adds Table 6 with experiments restricting observations per customer.

M1.justification: The correlated-probit model, best-of-three identification and estimation procedures, and empirical maximum-likelihood implementation remain unchanged. The added sparse-data experiment tests existing methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic data and sushi, jokes, Netflix and MovieLens datasets for the same tasks. Table 6 changes observation counts within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain intact in Tables 1–2, including the direct baseline in Table 2. The new Table 6 uses existing logit, matrix-completion and pairwise-probit baselines without replacing the original comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 6 adds a sampling condition with only three training observations and six validation observations per customer in rows marked split, alongside unrestricted reruns. The original evaluation protocols and Appendix F settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds a sensitivity analysis of limited observations per customer, testing whether matrix completion can adequately capture users under sparse data. Existing covariance-recovery, correlation and welfare analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy quantiles at 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75; Table 6 follows this practice. No new seed counts, replication design, confidence intervals or significance tests are specified.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–5 and figure results are retained. Table 6 adds rerun and restricted-observation results: for sushi A, matrix completion's median accuracy is 0.67 unrestricted versus 0.53 restricted, while best-of-three probit reports 0.67 versus 0.62. These are additional setting comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: The normalization and observability assumptions, identifiability theorems, finite-sample bounds, and proofs in Appendices B–E are retained. Mathematical differences inspected are typesetting changes rather than revised reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: pairwise-data insufficiency, best-of-three identifiability, efficient near-optimal estimation, and empirical benefits of modeling preference correlations.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly states that matrix completion needs many observations per user. Table 6 attributes deterioration under restricted observations to inadequate user modeling, adding an applicability qualification whose strongest demonstrated effects are on sushi.

D1.justification: V1's Section 6 code-repository footnote is removed without replacement in v2, reducing documented access information. This does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable. Existing Appendix F implementation and training details remain.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. Bibliographic formatting changes do not introduce new related work or novelty claims.

P1.justification: Limited prose edits clarify that independent Gumbel utility shocks imply IIA, add the observation-sparsity discussion, and update acknowledgments and publication text. The section organization and substantive narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR template throughout, changing typography, margins, running headers, the author block, table proportions and float placement. Figures 6–7 now share a page, and Table 6 is added. This is a document-wide visual revision, while existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Table 6 provides concrete evidence about a practical limitation of matrix completion that v1 discussed only generally, modestly improving interpretation of the comparisons. This gain is tempered by dataset-dependent effects and removal of the code-access link. The core theory and original experimental evidence remain unchanged.
